domain_assessment.domain: Fire-protection engineering for warehouse sprinkler retrofits
domain_assessment.role: Lead design engineer responsible for system redesign, hydraulic calculations, plan-review support, installation readiness, and commissioning
domain_assessment.objective: Develop a code-compliant sprinkler retrofit for high-piled rack storage, manage classification and hydraulic-design uncertainty, meet budget and approval requirements, and complete commissioning before tenant occupancy.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Retrospective account of four sequential engineering decisions involving incomplete hazard information, design-option selection, value engineering, and mandatory performance verification.

decision_points.summary: The participant classified the tenant's commodity as Class III before receiving tenant-specific SKU or packaging information.
evidence_before: The tenant had not finalized its SKU or packaging list.
The participant had the tenant's general business type and experience with two comparable 3PL clients.
The owner wanted a classification to establish the retrofit budget.
The participant reports that there was no schedule requirement to decide that week and that a preliminary packaging sample could have been requested.
evidence_after: A later partial inventory list indicated a greater presence of exposed unexpanded plastics than assumed.
The participant states that visible plastics information would have led to a more conservative classification.
goals_constraints: Determine the commodity classification driving density, area, and in-rack sprinkler requirements.
Enable the owner to establish a retrofit budget.
Work under incomplete tenant-specific inventory information.
Avoid unnecessary delay despite an extended six-week design window.
alternatives: Request a preliminary SKU or packaging sample and defer final classification.
Use a provisional conservative classification pending verification.
Use the Class III pattern inferred from two prior similar 3PL projects.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant relied on an expectation about what this type of 3PL tenant typically stores and chose that pattern over obtaining tenant-specific information.
decision_points.time_pressure: Not a compelling explanation. The participant explicitly states that they had time to request and await preliminary inventory information.
decision_points.uncertainty: The actual commodity and packaging mix, including the extent of exposed unexpanded plastics, was not known at the time of classification.

decision_points.summary: The participant selected the first density-and-area design point that met the assumed Class III code minimum and did not compare other configuration-specific alternatives.
evidence_before: Several density-and-area curve points would have met the assumed code minimum.
Some available alternatives would have required more in-rack sprinklers.
The participant could have compared alternatives against the rack configuration and aisle widths.
Manufacturer guidance tailored to the layout was available as a possible source.
Several weeks remained before permit submission.
evidence_after: The plan reviewer noted that the selected point was close to the applicable curve boundary for the actual rack configuration.
The participant acknowledges that they had time for further comparisons but did not revisit the selection after identifying an acceptable option.
goals_constraints: Produce a code-compliant hydraulic calculation package.
Select a design point appropriate to the actual rack arrangement.
Manage potential cost differences arising from additional in-rack sprinklers.
Use available design time to assess alternatives.
alternatives: Use the first point that cleared the assumed code minimum.
Compare multiple compliant density-and-area points against rack configuration and aisle widths.
Select a more conservative point with greater design margin.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant stopped the search process after finding the first option that worked under the assumed classification.
decision_points.time_pressure: Not a compelling explanation. The participant says there was time to run additional comparisons and that they simply did not loop back.
decision_points.uncertainty: There was unresolved uncertainty about the selected point's fit to the actual configuration, compounded by the upstream classification uncertainty.

decision_points.summary: The participant recommended removing the in-rack sprinkler allowance during value engineering to meet the owner's budget, while giving limited emphasis to the reduction in protection margin.
evidence_before: The owner requested value engineering because the design exceeded budget.
The in-rack sprinkler allowance was the largest identifiable cost item available to trim.
The participant knew that retaining the allowance would provide more margin against unresolved classification uncertainty.
The participant's firm had two further retrofit projects pending with the same owner.
evidence_after: The participant says that the classification uncertainty was mentioned but not described in depth.
The participant framed removal as a reasonable trade rather than explaining the degree of lost margin.
The participant acknowledges that the recommendation might have been different without the ongoing relationship.
goals_constraints: Bring the retrofit cost nearer to the owner's budget target.
Preserve adequate protection margin under unresolved classification uncertainty.
Maintain the firm's ongoing commercial relationship with the owner.
Communicate the tradeoff accurately enough for an informed owner decision.
alternatives: Recommend retaining the in-rack allowance and fully explain its uncertainty-related margin.
Recommend removing the allowance but fully quantify the protection-margin tradeoff.
Recommend removal while presenting it as a reasonable trade and minimizing the uncertainty discussion.
Identify another cost-reduction option that does not remove the same margin.
decision_points.decision_basis: The desire to avoid friction with a client who had future projects pending affected both the recommendation and the framing of the relevant risk.
decision_points.time_pressure: Not material to the stated reasoning mechanism.
decision_points.uncertainty: The upstream commodity classification remained uncertain, making the protection margin supplied by the allowance decision-relevant.

decision_points.summary: The participant completed the full AHJ-required witnessed flow test during commissioning.
evidence_before: The AHJ required a witnessed flow test.
The participant reports no reason to reduce the scope of testing.
evidence_after: The test passed comfortably above the required minimum.
The participant reports no concern about the commissioning choice.
goals_constraints: Verify actual system performance before occupancy.
alternatives: Perform the full witnessed flow test.
Attempt to abbreviate or rush the test, although no such action was taken and no operational basis for doing so is supplied.
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant followed the mandatory commissioning procedure because there was adequate time and no stated reason to reduce testing.
decision_points.uncertainty: System-performance uncertainty was appropriately addressed by the required witnessed test.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I'd done two other jobs for similar 3PL operators and had a good sense of what that kind of tenant typically stores. I went with Class III based on that pattern instead of waiting on their list.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision Point 1; initial incident description, followed by the probes concerning what information was available, whether the participant considered requesting it, and what would have prompted further inquiry.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant applied an inferred property of a tenant category—what a similar 3PL typically stores—to this particular tenant and substituted that category-based expectation for obtainable tenant-specific inventory and packaging evidence.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Prior cases involving genuinely similar tenants can provide legitimate analogical engineering evidence, particularly when inventory information is unavailable. The occurrence is nevertheless supported because the participant explicitly reports that tenant-specific verification was feasible, briefly considered it, and chose the generalized category pattern instead.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required for support. The transcript already establishes the category-based inference, the omitted tenant-specific evidence, and the availability of time to obtain that evidence.

revision.location: Decision Point 1, especially the participant answers beginning “There wasn't really a schedule reason” and “I went with that pattern instead of waiting on their list.”
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The classification episode contains an identifiable category-based inference and a feasible alternative evidentiary path.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the current local narrative and probes.
preserve: The six-week schedule and explicit absence of a need to classify that week.
The lack of a finalized SKU or packaging list at the time of classification.
The two prior comparable 3PL jobs as the source of the generalized expectation.
The later partial inventory information as post-decision context rather than as the primary proof of bias.
avoid_creating: Do not add another tenant-category inference at a later decision point.
Do not make the classification decision appear compelled by schedule scarcity.
Do not convert the episode into a generic information-availability failure without retaining the category-based reasoning.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I took the first point that cleared the minimum for the assumed classification and built the calc package around it. I had the time to run more comparisons, honestly, I just didn't loop back once I had something that worked.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision Point 2; the density-and-area selection answer following explicit identification of multiple compliant options, configuration-specific comparison opportunities, manufacturer guidance, and remaining schedule slack.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant adopted the first code-minimum-satisfying option as sufficient and prematurely stopped generating and comparing available alternatives, even though relevant layout-specific analysis could still have been performed.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Selecting a code-minimum solution can be professionally permissible, and engineers may reasonably avoid additional analysis when alternatives have little practical consequence. Here, the participant identifies several nonidentical alternatives, relevant configuration-specific evaluation methods, available time, and an explicit stopping rule of not returning after finding an option that worked.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required. The transcript directly identifies the first-acceptable stopping rule and differentiates it from schedule scarcity, ordinary calculation error, or a code violation.

revision.location: Decision Point 2, particularly the answer beginning “I took the first point that cleared the minimum.”
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The decision, alternatives, stopping rule, and absence of a binding time constraint are independently observable.
preserve: The availability of several compliant density-and-area points.
The possibility of comparing the points with actual rack configuration and aisle-width information.
The explicit statement that time remained for additional comparisons.
avoid_creating: Do not characterize the selected design point as noncompliant; the mechanism is premature stopping rather than rule violation.
Do not add a separate first-acceptable-option episode elsewhere in the interview.
Do not add schedule urgency that would supply an alternative explanation for the stopping rule.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “We've got two more retrofit jobs pending with him, and I didn't want friction over one line item, so I recommended pulling the allowance to hit his number.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision Point 3; the value-engineering account and follow-up probes about risk communication and whether the recommendation would have differed absent the ongoing client relationship.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant's interest in retaining future work and avoiding client friction affected the recommendation to remove a protection allowance and led to selective emphasis in communicating the risk associated with reduced margin.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Budget compliance and client-relationship management are ordinary commercial considerations and can properly inform value-engineering discussions. The occurrence is supported because the participant links the recommendation specifically to avoiding friction over future work and acknowledges communicating the uncertainty-related reduction in margin less fully than the decision warranted.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required. The transcript identifies the external incentive, the affected recommendation, the relevant safety-margin tradeoff, and the selective communication behavior.

revision.location: Decision Point 3, from the participant's explanation of the owner's budget request through the no-ongoing-relationship hypothetical.
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The relationship-linked motivation and its effect on both recommendation and risk communication are explicit.
preserve: The known classification uncertainty and the allowance's role as protection margin.
The distinction between the relationship-driven mechanism at this point and the schedule manipulation affecting Decision Points 1 and 2.
avoid_creating: Do not make the recommendation appear solely dictated by the owner; preserve the participant's discretionary recommendation and framing choice.
Do not introduce a new incentive-driven decision at another point.
Do not modify the relationship facts while preserving the counterfactual schedule manipulation.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Nothing in the early conversations flagged that, so it didn't feel urgent to chase down.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant may have treated an absence of salient warning cues as support for the pre-existing Class III expectation while not seeking potentially diagnostic tenant-specific information.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The statement may instead reflect ordinary triage of incomplete information. It does not show independent exposure to, interpretation of, or discounting of clearly disconfirming evidence. It is also closely embedded in the same reasoning episode as the supported category-based classification inference.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “I took the first point that cleared the minimum for the assumed classification and built the calc package around it.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The first satisfactory density-and-area point may have become an initial reference that discouraged further examination.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The evidence supports satisficing through premature stopping. It does not show that an arbitrary initial value distorted later judgments, estimates, or adjustments in a separately identifiable anchoring process.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “A partial inventory list came in later and showed more exposed unexpanded plastics mixed with the cartoned goods than I'd assumed.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A reviewer could mistakenly infer bias merely because later information showed that the initial classification was less conservative than it might have been.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The interview does not judge the original decision exclusively by its later outcome. It elicits the contemporaneous evidence, alternatives, and feasible verification opportunity, which are the proper basis for evaluating the classification reasoning.

nonbias_cues.cue: Later discovery of more exposed unexpanded plastics than assumed.
nonbias_cues.location: Decision Point 1, after the original classification.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The later inventory result indicates that the initial classification may have been insufficiently conservative, but an unfavorable later discovery is not itself evidence of cognitive bias. The supported finding rests on the contemporaneous category-based inference and bypassed verification opportunity.

nonbias_cues.cue: The plan reviewer's observation that the selected curve point was close to the edge of the applicable curve.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Reviewer concern or professional disagreement does not independently establish bias. It is corroborative context only; satisficing is supported by the participant's own account of stopping after finding the first acceptable option.

nonbias_cues.cue: The owner's request for a value-engineering pass because the design exceeded budget.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Budget pressure is an organizational and commercial constraint, not inherently a cognitive bias. It supports an incentive-bias interpretation only because the participant specifically links the recommendation and incomplete risk framing to preserving future work and avoiding client friction.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant's experience with two similar 3PL jobs.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Experienced pattern recognition can be justified expertise. It becomes evidence of stereotyping here only because the participant applied the category expectation to the current tenant in place of obtainable tenant-specific verification.

nonbias_cues.cue: Completion of the full required witnessed flow test.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The decision follows an AHJ requirement and adequate available time. A successful test result does not retrospectively validate or invalidate earlier decision processes, and no biased mechanism is evidenced at this point.

causal_claims.claim: The six-week schedule left enough time to seek tenant-specific inventory evidence before finalizing the commodity classification.
causal_claims.evidence: The participant states that there was no schedule reason to decide that week and that they could have asked for a preliminary packaging sample and waited.

causal_claims.claim: The six-week schedule left enough time to compare additional density-and-area options before finalizing the hydraulic package.
causal_claims.evidence: The participant states that there was plenty of runway, several alternatives were available, and they had time to run comparisons but did not loop back.

causal_claims.claim: The ongoing multi-project relationship affected the value-engineering recommendation and how the related risk was communicated.
causal_claims.evidence: The participant states that two pending projects and a desire to avoid friction influenced the recommendation, then acknowledges limited communication of lost margin and possible different behavior absent the relationship.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported, while recognizing that the no-relationship contrast is a qualified retrospective self-report.

causal_claims.claim: The initial classification influenced subsequent hydraulic-design and value-engineering reasoning.
causal_claims.evidence: The participant says classification drives density and rack-sprinkler requirements and later identifies classification uncertainty as the margin relevant to the allowance-removal decision.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported as a process dependency. The transcript should not be interpreted as establishing that classification was the sole cause of every subsequent design choice.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The later plastics information could produce hindsight-based attribution of the initial decision's quality solely from its later outcome.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: The interview elicits the information available at the time, the participant's generalized inference, and the feasible verification alternative.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The plan-review comment could be treated as proof of satisficing.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: The evidence for satisficing is the participant's stated first-acceptable stopping rule, multiple unexamined alternatives, and acknowledged available time; the reviewer comment is not the sole evidence.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The budget request could be confused with the incentive-bias mechanism.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: The interview separately identifies future projects, avoidance of friction, and selective risk communication as the relationship-linked mechanism.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Length of the design schedule before permit submission: the counterfactual scenario provides a six-week window rather than the paired scenario's three-week compressed window.
held_constant: The warehouse retrofit setting, tenant type, and high-piled rack configuration.
The existing water-supply and riser constraints.
The owner-set retrofit budget and value-engineering request.
The ongoing relationship between the engineering firm and the owner, including pending future work.
AHJ requirements for hydraulic calculations and the witnessed flow test.
The planned mapping of classification to Decision Point 1, density-and-area selection to Decision Point 2, value engineering to Decision Point 3, and commissioning to Decision Point 4.
causal_audit.explanation: The interview makes the changed schedule variable salient at the two decisions for which time scarcity might otherwise explain limited information seeking or reduced option comparison. It explicitly preserves the relationship-driven commercial mechanism at Decision Point 3 as independent of schedule length. Direct comparison with HE_Biased_3 is not possible because that paired interview is not supplied, but the present scenario is internally consistent with the specified counterfactual design.

global_revision_constraints: Preserve the exactly four-decision-point structure and the allocation of one target occurrence each to Decision Points 1, 2, and 3.
Preserve the six-week schedule slack and the explicit absence of a calendar-based necessity to decide immediately at Decision Points 1 and 2.
Preserve the owner relationship and pending-project context as the Decision Point 3 incentive mechanism, independent of the schedule manipulation.
Do not elevate the weak confirmation-bias cue into a separate occurrence unless the manifest is intentionally expanded.
Keep the commissioning episode at Decision Point 4 neutral, mandatory, and free of an intentional bias occurrence.

failure_flags.detail: The interview is internally coherent with the stated counterfactual manipulation, but the paired HE_Biased_3 interview is not provided, so exact cross-scenario constancy of the incentive-bias wording and all other held variables cannot be independently verified.
